title: Nacha roles: sponsor as Originator, Unbound as Third-Party Service Provider holding no funds
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Each program records a role table naming the Originator (the sponsor), the ODFI, Third-Party Service Providers (Unbound), any Third-Party Sender or grant-rail partner, and the authorization holder (CNV-PAY-001). By default the sponsor is Originator of record on sponsor-titled accounts under its own ODFI agreement; the platform operator is a Third-Party Service Provider, never a Third-Party Sender, and holds no funds (UNB-XIN-BNK-001). Unbound does not sign an origination agreement, hold or pool donor or grant money, or execute or block a payment on its own authority; any configuration that would do so is rejected, and a funds-flow conformance check blocks activation of any deployment that fails (CNV-PAY-001, CNV-LEG-001, UNB-XIN-REG-001). Unbound accepts TPSP obligations by contract, including Nacha risk-based fraud monitoring, data security and audit cooperation. A versioned RailObligation register maps every binding obligation for each rail and role to a control, and production enablement of any rail must pass a RailGoLive gate (RR-UNB-PAY-008-r1). Outbound payments are deliberately deferred: no rail, bank or provider is selected and no live payment is authorized (PAY-DEF-001 in DEFERRED-PAYMENTS-AND-REMAINING-GAPS.md).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Complete funds-flow legal review and ODFI engagement per sponsor before any rail is enabled; publish the role table to each sponsor's ODFI.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirements text can be shown: CNV-PAY-001, UNB-XIN-BNK-001, CNV-LEG-001, UNB-XIN-REG-001, RR-UNB-PAY-008-r1, UNB-PAY-008 in unbound@9b38de47:requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl. No test, operating evidence or auditor review exists.
customer_statement: Unbound does not process live payments. Its requirements define the sponsor as Originator and Unbound as a Third-Party Service Provider that never holds funds or originates on its own authority. No rail or bank relationship exists yet.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority
residual_risks: Role classification depends on facts each ODFI and counsel will assess; if Unbound transmits files to the ODFI on the sponsor's behalf, some banks may analyze it as closer to a Third-Party Sender arrangement.
open_questions: CNV-LEG-001 says Unbound SHALL NOT be able to execute a payment, while UNB-XIN-REG-001 gives the operator instruction-only authority and the dispatcher transmits instructions (UNB-XIN-EVA-011, CNV-ARC-003). Clarify with counsel whether transmitting sponsor-authorized files is consistent with the TPSP characterization and with 'cannot execute'.

challenge.customer_intent: ODFI and sponsor want clarity on who bears Nacha warranties and liabilities and whether the vendor is a Third-Party Sender requiring its own agreement and audit.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Misclassified role leads to missing agreements, unmet audit obligations or unexpected vendor liability.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Many payment vendors act as Third-Party Senders with pooled accounts, which concentrates risk and requires stronger oversight.
challenge.legally_required: Nacha Operating Rules (contractual) define the roles; money transmission law may apply if a vendor holds funds.
challenge.contractually_required: ODFI origination agreements and TPSP contracts.
challenge.historical_convention: Vendor-held FBO or pooled accounts as Third-Party Sender.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Within conforming deployments, vendor custody of funds is eliminated: no operator-titled accounts exist (CNV-LEG-001).
challenge.continuous_evidence: Role table and FundsFlow declaration versions.
challenge.stronger_alternative: TPSP-only model with sponsor-titled accounts and sponsor-held ODFI relationships.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through account titling evidence and ODFI agreements.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely for sponsors with existing bank relationships; harder for small sponsors without ACH origination capability.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: A sponsor without an ODFI agreement, or a rail partner that pools funds.
challenge.conventional_cost: Licensing and compliance cost if the vendor holds funds.
challenge.alternative_risks: Operational dependence on each sponsor's bank capabilities.
supporting_arguments: Keeps legal control of DAF assets with the sponsor.
opposing_arguments: Some ODFIs may still treat a file-transmitting vendor as a Third-Party Sender.
Small sponsors may prefer a vendor-originated model.

title: ACH debit authorizations, retention, account validation and return-rate monitoring
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Release 1 does not originate ACH debits from donors; contributions arrive by ACH credit, wire, check, securities transfer or the sponsor's existing processor (CNV-PAY-005). When donor debit origination is enabled, the system captures a signed or similarly authenticated authorization stating amount or range, frequency, start date, debiting entity and revocation method, delivers a copy, gives at least 10 days' notice of out-of-range amounts and honors revocation for entries not yet sent (UNB-XIN-PAY-001). Authorizations are retained for their active life plus two years after termination or revocation and are not deleted while warranty claims may arise (CNV-PAY-005). The first WEB debit to an account, and the first after any change, requires account validation by prenote, micro-entry or a third-party service (UNB-XIN-PAY-002). Rolling 60-day unauthorized, administrative and overall return rates are computed per Originator with alerts at configurable fractions of the Nacha thresholds and automatic suspension above a sponsor hard limit; reinitiation is allowed only for R01 and R09 (and R02 to R04 after correction), at most twice within 180 days, with 'RETRY PYMT' and identical company name, ID and amount (UNB-XIN-PAY-005).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Keep donor debit origination disabled until the RailGoLive gate passes for a sponsor; implement authorization records under a retention class that cannot expire during warranty windows.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirements text can be shown: CNV-PAY-005, UNB-XIN-PAY-001, UNB-XIN-PAY-002, UNB-XIN-PAY-005 in unbound@9b38de47:requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl. No test, operating evidence or auditor review exists.
customer_statement: Unbound will not originate donor ACH debits in its first release. When enabled, authorization capture, retention for two years after revocation, account validation and return-rate monitoring are specified. Not implemented.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority
open_questions: Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.10) governs preauthorized transfers from consumer accounts; it is not yet in the seeded source list.

title: ACH returns and notifications of change
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Returns match on original entry trace number, return reason code and return trace; NOCs match on original trace, change code and COR trace. When addenda are missing a fallback match (amount, effective date, company ID, account last four, individual ID) routes to a queue and never auto-posts (CNV-PAY-005). These keys are the registered business idempotency keys, so redelivered files have no second effect (UNB-XIN-EVA-005). NOC corrections apply within six banking days or before the next entry, whichever is later, under change control; a matched bank-originated NOC counts as destination evidence without cooling-off but notifies the charity's verified channels, while any charity-requested change triggered by an NOC follows the full destination-change rule (CNV-PAY-002). Returns are accepted even after a grant is Disbursed or Final where the rail permits (TVR-GR-002); returned grant funds re-credit the originating fund by linked compensating entry, generate no acknowledgment, and restore capacity only after reconciliation (UNB-RCN-GRT-015). Return and NOC matching apply to grant payments from release 1.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Build return and NOC ingestion with deterministic matching, an exception queue and an NOC application timer.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirements text can be shown: CNV-PAY-005, CNV-PAY-002, UNB-XIN-EVA-005, TVR-GR-002, UNB-RCN-GRT-015, RR-UNB-PAY-006-r1 in unbound@9b38de47:requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl. No test, operating evidence or auditor review exists.
customer_statement: Planned: returns and NOCs are specified to match deterministically on trace keys, with unmatched items queued for people and NOC corrections applied within Nacha timeframes under change control. Not implemented.

title: Wire transfers, UCC Article 4A security procedures and irrevocable rails
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Rails are governed by a versioned RailEligibility matrix keyed by payment class, rail and direction, with per-payment and daily limits and an irreversibility class; Irrevocable and RequestOnly rails such as wires require independent destination confirmation for each payment above a threshold, and instant rails default to not allowed for grants until a sponsor enables them (UNB-XIN-BNK-004). Domestic wires are sent with no-deduction instructions and international wires default to OUR charges, with any pass-through disclosed (CNV-PAY-007). Wire outcomes are confirmed by Fedwire IMAD/OMAD and beneficiary-bank confirmation before final aging (CNV-PAY-004). An adverse sanctions or status event on a dispatched but unsettled payment automatically triggers a recall request recorded as externally uncertain (UNB-RCN-GRT-016). Because the sponsor is the bank's customer under Article 4A, the commercially reasonable security procedure is agreed between the sponsor and its bank; Unbound's role is to deliver only independently approved instructions through an authenticated channel the sponsor's bank recognizes.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Document, per sponsor, how Unbound-delivered wire instructions interact with the sponsor's Article 4A security procedure, and keep account-number and beneficiary-name consistency checks before release.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirements text can be shown: UNB-XIN-BNK-004, CNV-PAY-007, CNV-PAY-004, UNB-RCN-GRT-016, UNB-CUST-008 in unbound@9b38de47:requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl. No test, operating evidence or auditor review exists.
customer_statement: Planned: wires are specified as irrevocable-class payments with independent destination confirmation, limits and confirmation tracking. No wire capability exists, and Unbound's requirements do not yet address Article 4A security procedure agreements explicitly.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority
open_questions: No Unbound requirement addresses the Article 4A security procedure between sponsor and bank, or loss allocation when a verified instruction comes through Unbound. Recommend a requirement.

title: Check issuance, void handling, stale dating and reissue
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: The check rail models Issued, Outstanding, AgedOutreach, StaleDated, VoidRequested, VoidConfirmed, Cleared and UnclaimedPropertyReportable, each with a defined grant, reservation and ledger effect (UNB-RCN-GRT-005). Positive pay with daily issue files including voids is mandatory, and a check is mailed only after the bank acknowledges its issue record (CNV-PAY-002, UNB-XIN-BNK-006). Checks void by default at 90 days, configurable but never later than the shortest applicable state window, with a recorded reason; voiding does not extinguish the grant obligation and does not automatically re-credit the fund (CNV-PAY-002). A reissue requires a confirmed stop or void, verified recipient eligibility and destination, and a linked replacement chain (UNB-RCN-GRT-005, CNV-PAY-004). Every program keeps a check fallback and stored verified destination so charities outside partner networks can be paid (CNV-PAY-001).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Implement the check state machine with void acknowledgment and reissue chain; print and mail through a vendor or the sponsor's bank (not selected).

title: Unclaimed property for uncashed grant and refund checks
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Unbound maintains a counsel-approved UnclaimedPropertyRule table per state covering owner type, property type, dormancy period, business-to-business or charitable exemption flags, due-diligence notice window and content, and report and remittance dates; the state is determined by the payee's last known address with the sponsor's state of incorporation as fallback per counsel (UNB-XIN-BNK-007). Outstanding uncashed grant checks are presumed reportable property owed to the payee charity; before dormancy the system makes two outreach attempts including an offer to reissue by ACH. Void-and-re-credit to the fund is permitted only if the grant was cancelled before cashing with notice to the charity and the state row records that cancellation defeats the holder obligation. A VoidDisposition record decides re-credit, hold as payable or report; unknown inputs default to Hold and report at dormancy, and business-to-business exemptions default to not applicable to grants (CNV-PAY-003). Items with no applicable rule stay in review and are never re-credited.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Populate state rule rows from statute text starting with states where sponsors concentrate; generate report and remittance data for the sponsor as holder.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirements text can be shown: UNB-XIN-BNK-007, CNV-PAY-003, UNB-RCN-GRT-005, UNB-RCN-ENT-005 in unbound@9b38de47:requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl. No test, operating evidence or auditor review exists.

title: Payment file security and bank integration authentication
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Every bank, payment-partner and custodian integration documents its authentication method, credential rotation, least privilege, webhook signature verification, replay defense, partner context binding and outage behavior (UNB-API-STD-005, UNB-CUST-017). Inbound files and callbacks require verifiable origin, freshness, deduplication, ordering and replay protection (UNB-CUST-009, RR-REQ-X-083-r1). Credentials are scoped per sponsor; secrets are never hardcoded and are managed with approved libraries, managed keys, scanning and rotation (SEC-CRYPTO-001). Sandbox tenants are bound to mock adapters and cannot resolve or authenticate to any production bank, payment or custody endpoint, and the simulated adapter never calls a real rail (UNB-XIN-SAS-010, UNB-SCTRL-030). Payment data, including account numbers, is classified and encrypted under the platform data policy (SOC2-014), and Unbound would accept Nacha data security obligations as a TPSP (CNV-PAY-001).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Select per-bank transport (bank API with mutual TLS or signed requests, or SFTP with file-level encryption and signing as the bank supports); keep integration credentials in a managed secret store with per-sponsor scope.

title: Dual control on payment release, limits and no out-of-band origination
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: No grant recommendation, AI proposal or internal journal authorizes outbound funds; release requires sponsor reserved authority, independent release control, payee verification and least privilege (UNB-PAY-003). Until a deterministic release gate is accepted by the sponsor's auditor and board, release requires three distinct people (CNV-GOV-003). Approvals are checked against delegation-of-authority limits, and rail eligibility carries per-payment and daily limits (UNB-XIN-ERP-005, UNB-XIN-BNK-004). A batch carries no approval or release authority itself; each item is released and re-checked against holds immediately before transmission (UNB-XIN-EVA-011, CNV-ARC-003). No payment may originate outside the platform gate, manual fallback runs through the gate with dual control, and bank portal entitlements give no unilateral release rights outside it (TVR-PAY-004). When bank feeds are stale, releases of already-reserved grants may proceed only on a balance attestation by two treasury staff distinct from the releasing approvers, valid one business day (CNV-PAY-007). Any platform hold leaves the sponsor able to pay through its own bank channel (CNV-PLT-007).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Implement the release gate with distinct-person enforcement and limit checks; document each sponsor's bank portal entitlement configuration and review it quarterly.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure no single person can send money.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Single-person fraud or error in payment release.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Dual approval in the bank portal is standard but often undermined by shared tokens, broad entitlements and rubber-stamping.
challenge.legally_required: No statute; bank agreements and auditor expectations.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly in bank agreements and sponsor policies.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Within the platform, single-person release is impossible because the gate requires distinct principals; out-of-band release is addressed by limiting portal entitlements, which Unbound cannot enforce.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Distinct-person check, limits and hold re-check at transmission.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Release records with approvers, limits and hold versions per item.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Platform gate as the only release path, bank portal limited to view and emergency use under dual control, plus daily unmatched-debit detection.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partly: platform gate is verifiable; portal entitlements require sponsor and bank evidence.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely; some sponsors will want to keep portal release rights.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Sponsor keeps broad portal release entitlements.
challenge.alternative_cost: Medium; operational dependence on platform availability.
challenge.alternative_risks: Outage blocks payments unless an emergency procedure exists (open question).
supporting_arguments: Closes the organizational double-payment and bypass path.
opposing_arguments: Sponsors and banks may require retaining portal-based release.
